```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B names a payer and a price anchored to sourced, live listings: Bulletin at $3.99/mo, $19.99/yr and $39.99 lifetime, and Ground News at $9.99/mo and $99.99/yr. A's own Payer section says 'No clean single payer found.' Every A competitor is free and funded by grants, VC, ads or nonprofit dues.",
    "The goal is one paying customer within 90 days, not a durable business. B's evidence shows consumers can be charged for this feature set: there are live IAP tiers, and a Syft reviewer said 'Revert the UI back and I'll pay.' A's only monetization analog, Pointz, needed $520k in outside funding and does not publish its subscription price.",
    "B's competitors show single developers have shipped and listed paid tiers in this category. A's own Case Against says a solo six-week build has 'no seed data and no existing relationship' with the municipalities or advocacy groups that A's alternative payer path depends on.",
    "A's demand evidence shows people want to report hazards, through tools like WABA, BikeMaps.org and LaneSpotter. None of it shows anyone paying a third party for that function. Demand without a payer does not meet a 90-day revenue goal.",
    "A carries ongoing liability and moderation costs tied to safety-critical data, flagged in its Case Against and Regulatory Setup. B's regulatory burden is mostly a one-time IP consult plus platform self-declaration forms.",
    "B's risks are serious but mostly hit long-term scale, not a first sale: saturation with at least five near-clones, Artifact's shutdown, and AI news features being folded free into Apple News, Google News and chatbots."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's Case For claims a 'credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants)' with no source. The brief's own evidence contradicts it. BikeMaps.org's grant went to a research project, not to buying a vendor's tool. WABA runs its own free tracker. Open Question 1 admits it is unknown whether cities or nonprofits would pay for a third-party tool. Treated as unsourced, this leaves A with no evidenced payer at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. B wins mainly because A has no evidenced payer, not because B's revenue evidence is strong. B shows that list prices exist, but no brief shows actual subscriber counts or conversion. The Syft quote is conditional, and the Artifact case plus heavy saturation suggest retention and paid acquisition will be hard. B is the better first bet for one paying customer in 90 days. It is not clearly a better long-term business."
}
```
